- Sample pH 5 (slightly acidic). Multi-colored flame indicates multiple cations with characteristic flame colors present. Flame colors list: Ba (green), Ca (orange-red), Cs (blue-violet), Cu (turquoise), K (pale violet), Li (red), Na (yellow), Rb (red-violet), Sr (red). Multi-colored suggests at least two of these present.

- Adding KOH(0.05M) gave precipitate thistle/white. Thistle color corresponds to Mn3(PO4)2 (thistle) per precipitate colors list. Also white precipitate could be many. Thistle indicates presence of Mn3+? Actually Mn3(PO4)2 is thistle. So Mn present? But KOH would precipitate metal hydroxides: Mn(OH)2 is pale pink, not thistle. Thistle is phosphate precipitate, but KOH alone no phosphate. Maybe thistle is due to Mn3(PO4)2 formed from reaction with phosphate impurity? Not likely. Could be due to presence of Ni? Ni3(PO4)2 is pale green. So thistle is Mn3(PO4)2. But KOH alone shouldn't give phosphate. Could be that sample contains phosphate anion, leading to precipitation of metal phosphate with K+? Actually K+ doesn't precipitate. So maybe the thistle is due to formation of Mn(OH)2? But color list shows Mn(OH)2 pale pink. So thistle maybe due to Mn3(PO4)2 from reaction with phosphate present in sample? Not sure.

- DMG test gave white precipitate. DMG forms red precipitate with Ni2+ (Ni(DMG)2). White precipitate indicates no Ni2+.

- K2CrO4 gave yellow precipitate, supernatant pale yellow. Yellow precipitate could be BaCrO4, CaCrO4, CdCrO4, PbCrO4, SrCrO4, ZnCrO4. Since K2CrO4 provides CrO4^2- which precipitates with Ba2+, Ca2+, Pb2+, Sr2+, Zn2+, Cd2+. So one of those cations present.

- Adding HCl(1M) to the K2CrO4 precipitate dissolved, solution turned light yellow. That suggests the precipitate was soluble in acid, typical for BaCrO4? BaCrO4 is slightly soluble in strong acid? Actually BaCrO4 is insoluble in acid? I think BaCrO4 dissolves in strong acid forming H2CrO4 and Ba2+. Many chromate precipitates dissolve in acid. So could be Ba2+, Ca2+, Pb2+, Sr2+, Zn2+, Cd2+. Need further test.

- NH3(5M) gave pale pink precipitate. Pink precipitate with NH3 suggests formation of Cu(OH)2? Actually Cu(OH)2 is blue. Co(OH)2 is blue. Ni(OH)2 pale green. Mn(OH)2 pale pink. So pale pink indicates Mn(OH)2. So Mn2+ present.

Thus we have Mn2+.

- Flame test multi-colored suggests other cations with flame colors. Mn has no flame color.

- K2CrO4 precipitate indicates one of Ba, Ca, Pb, Sr, Zn, Cd. Need differentiate.

We can test with H2S (acidic) to see sulfide precipitates: PbS black, CdS yellowish orange, ZnS white? Actually ZnS is white? Not listed (white). So color will help.

We have reagents: H2S(acidic) (contains H2S 0.1M + HCl 0.05M). Use that.

Also we have (NH4)2S (basic) maybe.

Let's test with H2S(acidic) on filtrate (which contains the cation that formed chromate precipitate). Use test.
